business_context.ambition: Establish LOA as a distinctive adult soft drink for bright social occasions, then prove a repeatable route from trial to repeat purchase before scaling media or distribution.
business_context.business_model: Fictional founder-led premium low-sugar soft drinks brand, with direct-to-consumer and selective wholesale routes
known_constraints: No real LOA client analytics, accounts or retailer sell-through supplied
No verified customer, category or competitor research specific to LOA supplied
No approved production, distribution or media budget supplied
All LOA commercial inputs are assumptions; real external evidence only describes market context

unresolved_inputs: Actual net contribution by SKU and channel
Sampling, production, distribution and media cost
Monthly ramp, seasonality, stock and working capital

creative_territory.asset_alt: Internal AI-generated coral LOA bottle with gold cap and cream lettering, supplied through Claude's existing LOA asset work
creative_territory.description: Coral glass, gold cap and cream LOA lettering remain the visual anchor. Each execution starts in an ordinary low-energy moment, then the bottle, pour and shared serve introduce warmth, sound and appetite. This is an internal illustration, not evidence of a real product or campaign.
creative_territory.example_execution: A six-second film opens on the flat hum of a convenience-store cooler. A coral LOA bottle is lifted, opened and poured beside a late lunch; the scene warms as the bubbles rise. End frame: POUR BRIGHTER. No performance, health, stockist or product claim is made.
creative_territory.name: A Brighter Pour
creative_territory.platform: Turn the small social pause into something vivid: an unmistakable LOA pour, served with food, colour and a little ceremony.
principles: Bottle, opening and pour are the mnemonic
Food, glass, bubbles and condensation stay tactile
Colour arrives through the serve, not visual noise
creative_territory.validation_test: Test product recognition, occasion comprehension, brand attribution, appetite, distinctiveness and legal clearance before any external production.

evidence_gaps: Founder-authorised revenue, units, channel mix, tax, returns, discounts and contribution
Product formulation, claims substantiation and regulatory review
Customer occasions, preference, repeat, willingness to pay and audience definition
Retailer sell-through, distribution terms, stock capacity and production lead time
Competitor positioning, price architecture, share of shelf and creative activity
Quoted activation production, sampling, media and measurement cost

evidence_ledger.claim: The UK government announced that the lower Soft Drinks Industry Levy sugar threshold will reduce from 5g to 4.5g per 100ml from January 2028.
evidence_ledger.limitations: This is category regulation, not evidence of LOA formulation, demand or performance.
evidence_ledger.publisher: HM Treasury and HM Revenue & Customs
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Confirm the final legislation and verify LOA recipes independently before making any formulation claim.

evidence_ledger.claim: The UK government reported a 46% average reduction in sugar content in in-scope soft drinks between 2015 and 2020.
evidence_ledger.limitations: Historical category reformulation does not establish consumer demand for LOA or any individual brand.
evidence_ledger.publisher: HM Treasury and HM Revenue & Customs
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Use the latest official category data and obtain product-level evidence before commercial use.

evidence_ledger.claim: The British Soft Drinks Association's 2025 annual report states that more than seven in ten UK soft drinks sold are low or no sugar.
evidence_ledger.limitations: This is an industry-body category statistic and does not verify LOA's market, audience or sales potential.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Recheck the original report and triangulate with independent retail and customer evidence.

evidence_ledger.claim: LOA receives 180,000 ecommerce sessions per year.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No authorised analytics export exists for this fictional company.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Reconcile an authorised GA4 export to ecommerce sessions and orders.

evidence_ledger.claim: LOA converts 1.8% of ecommerce sessions to orders.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No analytics or order export exists for this fictional company.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Agree the denominator and reconcile sessions to completed non-refunded orders.

evidence_ledger.claim: LOA has a £32 average ecommerce order value before returns, discounts and VAT treatment.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No transaction export or pack architecture has been supplied.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Calculate realised order value from an authorised transaction export.

evidence_ledger.claim: LOA's principal growth constraint is an attractive visual identity without a sufficiently specific occasion, proposition or trial-to-repeat system.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No founder interview, customer research, funnel data or retailer evidence supports this diagnosis.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Run founder interviews, occasion research, proposition testing and a controlled conversion test.

evidence_ledger.claim: LOA could build an advantage by pairing its distinctive bottle with a clear role as the bright adult soft drink for social pauses.
evidence_ledger.limitations: Distinctiveness, relevance, ownability and willingness to pay are untested.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Test the territory against category alternatives with target customers and trade buyers.

evidence_ledger.claim: A city-led sampling, selective wholesale, DTC replenishment and CRM growth engine is operationally feasible.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No distribution terms, stock capacity, cohort data, media economics or sampling costs exist.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Obtain contribution, capacity, distribution and cohort data before any activation.

evidence_ledger.claim: Incremental ecommerce revenue contributes 30% after product, fulfilment, payment, returns and incremental media costs.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No channel or product contribution data exists for this fictional company.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Reconcile order-level net revenue and variable cost by product and channel.

evidence_ledger.claim: LOA could realise 30% to 60% of annualised ecommerce scenario headroom during the first 12 months.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No launch cadence, seasonality, stock or distribution plan supports this range.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Build a monthly plan with test velocity, stock capacity and seasonality.

evidence_ledger.claim: The first 12 months require £65,000 of incremental implementation investment beyond the £5,000 Growth Blueprint fee.
evidence_ledger.limitations: No supplier, production, sampling, distribution or media quotes exist.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Obtain a costed activation plan before approval.

evidence_ledger.claim: A Brighter Pour is an illustrative campaign territory for fictional LOA.
evidence_ledger.limitations: It has not been approved by a client, tested with customers or cleared legally.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Check strategic fit, distinction, comprehension and legal availability.

evidence_ledger.claim: Claude's existing LOA coral bottle hero and convenience-store film are reused as internal creative illustrations.
evidence_ledger.limitations: Existing internal AI-generated assets do not depict real LOA products, stockists, customers or campaigns.
evidence_ledger.validation_step: Matt must confirm source provenance, usage rights, product accuracy and client-facing suitability.

channels.gate: Stockist economics, weekly sell-through and reorder
channels.role: Place LOA inside the target occasion and observe sell-through

channels.gate: Permission, sample-to-site capture, cost and product feedback
channels.role: Create qualified first taste around food, design and culture

channels.gate: Net conversion, second purchase, opt-out and contribution
channels.role: Convert mixed-case trial into measured replenishment

channels.gate: Incremental contribution after production and media cost
channels.role: Scale only the creative and occasions already linked to repeat

measurement.metrics: Brand attribution, occasion comprehension, qualified sample-to-site and retailer availability
Net conversion, mixed-case uptake, second purchase, retailer sell-through and reorder
Contribution after product, fulfilment, sampling, production, media and distribution

growth_engine.scale_gate: Release media or wider distribution only when a defined occasion improves trial quality and repeat contribution without unacceptable discounting, waste, stock risk or retailer churn.
growth_engine.thesis: Use one city and a small number of food-led occasions to connect observed trial, DTC capture, replenishment and retailer sell-through before any national awareness spend.

constraint_content.left_detail: Distinctive visual assets are useful, but not proof of demand or repeat.

customer_evidence_content.interpretation: The territory remains a hypothesis until customer choice and repeat evidence support it.

presentation.destination_takeaway: LOA could become the vivid adult soft drink for social pauses, if one ownable occasion can turn first taste into profitable repeat.
presentation.falsification_takeaway: The diagnosis fails if LOA already owns a clear occasion and existing cohorts repeat profitably without heavier discounting.

market_gap_content.audience: Adults seeking a grown-up soft option; definition requires research
market_gap_content.competitor_miss: No competitor position is asserted until research is completed.
market_gap_content.market_gap: A vivid adult soft-drink ritual for everyday social pauses

presentation.strategic_moves_takeaway: Own the brighter pause, make the pour the proof, then turn concentrated trial into measured repeat.

strategy_framework_content.banner: Give LOA one social job, then make the pour earn the next purchase.
steps: A memorable bottle without a proven buying occasion
Make the LOA pour the recognisable ritual
Link concentrated trial to measured repeat before reach

presentation.subtitle: A conditional route from distinctive bottle to repeatable demand

roadmap.decision_gate: Matt approves one bounded proposition and evidence plan; no media or production spend is released.
roadmap.name: Establish the truth
roadmap.outcome: Verify unit economics, formulation and availability; interview founder, customers and trade; test three occasion propositions.

roadmap.decision_gate: Continue only if attribution, trial quality, repeat and unit contribution pass agreed thresholds.
roadmap.name: Prove the brighter pour
roadmap.outcome: Run controlled creative, sampling, DTC capture and one-city wholesale tests using approved claims and assets.
roadmap.owner: Creative Director and Growth Strategy Director

roadmap.decision_gate: Approve expansion only when stock, contribution, repeat and retailer economics support it.
roadmap.name: Build the repeat system
roadmap.outcome: Codify winning serve, content, CRM, replenishment and retailer reorder mechanics.

roadmap.decision_gate: Matt approves every material commercial commitment and exact client-facing or public release.
roadmap.name: Scale selectively
roadmap.outcome: Expand only the verified occasions, postcodes, stockists and creative routes, with holdouts and stop rules.

advantage.statement: LOA could turn its coral bottle and optimistic visual language into a recognisable adult soft-drink ritual: a brighter pour for social pauses that deserve more than water and less than alcohol.
advantage.validation_test: Compare A Brighter Pour with taste-led, wellness-led and alcohol-alternative routes on relevance, distinctiveness, credibility, recall and willingness to pay.

constraint.falsification_test: Reject this diagnosis if founder, customer and cohort evidence already shows a clear occasion, strong unprompted proposition recall and profitable repeat without increased discounting.
constraint.statement: LOA may have a memorable bottle, but it has not yet proved the specific occasion, reason to choose or route from first taste to profitable repeat.

recommendations.action: Define and test LOA around the moments when adults want a vivid, grown-up soft drink without making an unverified health or alcohol-replacement claim.
recommendations.name: Own the brighter pause
recommendations.test: Founder interview, occasion research and controlled proposition test
recommendations.trade_off: A sharper occasion excludes generic refreshment traffic and must earn credibility.

recommendations.action: Use the bottle, serve, sound, colour and food pairing as recurring evidence of the occasion rather than relying on abstract lifestyle imagery.
recommendations.name: Make the pour the proof
recommendations.test: Creative recognition, comprehension and qualified sample-to-site test
recommendations.trade_off: Product-centred work will reveal any weakness in taste, pack, serve or availability.

recommendations.action: Concentrate sampling and selective wholesale where repeat can be observed, then use DTC mixed cases and CRM replenishment to measure second purchase.
recommendations.name: Turn trial into repeat
recommendations.test: One-city cohort test of repeat and retailer sell-through
recommendations.trade_off: Geographic focus slows broad awareness while protecting cash and learning quality.

strategy.thesis: Give LOA one ownable social job, make the bright-pour ritual unmistakable, then connect selective trial to measured repeat before buying reach.
